Right now, gift cards and promo codes can only be made on the Pelham Hills admin pages. The GPS app has just the stamp book, one free round for every ten, and a guest's phone never shows the cards or coupons they were given. The plan is to issue from the GPS app too, and let guests pull them up in the app.

The key rule is one ledger. The GPS app and the pro shop share the same database. So the GPS app adds no new tables: it writes to the same gift card and promotion tables, through the same functions the pro shop uses. Wherever a card is issued, the barcode and the balance are the same.

Issuing happens in a new tab on the GPS admin page, Coupons and Gift Cards. Only manager accounts that can already issue gift cards at the pro shop see it. It is the same sign-in, so no separate permission is needed. The shared proshop account and admins who only edit the course map cannot see it.

There are three things to issue. A gift card has an amount, its balance goes down as it is used, and it never expires. A personal coupon is new: a one-time discount tied to one guest, with an expiry date. A campaign coupon is a shared code, like today's promo codes.

The coupon screen in the guest app becomes a wallet. Gift cards with their balance sit on top, coupons with expiry dates below, and today's stamp book at the bottom. Tap one and the barcode fills the screen. Guests without the app still get the barcode by text, as they do now.

Checkout stays the same. Scan the barcode on a pro shop bill: a gift card goes in as the payment method, a coupon as a green fee discount. Once the bill is paid, the balance and coupon status in the guest's app change right away, and a notification tells them what is left.

Here is how to run it. When a complaint call comes in, the manager sends a complimentary gift card straight to that guest's app. When rain stops a round, give a personal coupon instead of a rain check. At the holidays, take payment at the pro shop and issue a sold card. For guests who haven't been back in a while, the manager reviews the list and sends a come-back coupon.

The safeguards carry over. A reason is required to issue, a gift card tops out at five thousand dollars, and voiding needs a reason too. Issued cards go out in a daily email. The order: run the 0120 SQL first, decide on personal coupons, then build the 0121 functions and the GPS screens and deploy. Pushing to the GPS repository still needs access.
